Native matrix invokes the actual helper directly in fresh CI. Exporter uses temporary source/config and a synthetic account, with remote metadata disabled and blocked external proxies. This is narrower than the separate next_test environment allowlist and is not an OS network sandbox.

Capability stage nonzero exit fails the job; subsequent always stages preserve the outcome and upload available reports. A passing summary writer does not convert a failed capability stage into a passed job.

limitations: Approved offline means this guard and its stated evidence boundary were reviewed; it is not semantic approval for every accepted interface change, a live-equivalence conclusion, or release acceptance.
No native Linux/Windows GitHub job or complete macOS CI job was executed by this review. Native platform behavior requires actual workflow artifacts.

The exporter captures declarations and command registration presence, not every dynamic behavior, HTTP effect, help description or plugin-supplied command. Separate exact-source reviews and operation tests remain required.

The mapping is controlled repository data requiring review for intentional changes. Passing a regenerated mapping does not independently justify a change; the documented exact-review process is part of its maintenance boundary.
Snapshot evidence covers tracked source bytes. Untracked source is disclosed and excluded by the exporter; invocation-time cleanup/report failures outside supported handled outcomes remain explicit.
Environment/proxy isolation is not a network sandbox. The capability stage relies on fresh credential-free CI plus synthetic exporter account/config and executes no business commands.
Prior CI1–CI4 review and closure artifacts remain unchanged. Their native-cleanup/report destination limitations continue to apply to the separate suite runner.
